name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
pitch: A mixture-of-experts model that reads only a few experts a token, in turboderp's EXL3 packs, with its own draft layer.
architecture: 48 layers (36 Gated DeltaNet, 12 sparse-attention), each a mixture of 512 experts of which 10 and a shared one run a token (about 121B of the parameters), four hyper-connection streams, a hashed n-gram embedding (PLE) and one multi-token-prediction layer that drafts for speculation.
license: The model's license is on its Hugging Face page. TandemLLM itself is AGPL-3.0 or commercial.

devices.label: NVIDIA DGX Spark (128 GB unified memory)
devices.note: The GPU and the CPU share this memory. MemTotal reads 121.6 GiB of the 128 GB.

assets.source: Public on Hugging Face; install.sh --setup downloads it for Wren, the fetch step when the narrator is on (VIS-153).

measurements.method: The ENG-229 A/B's served arm on 3.05: one fresh server, prompts prose / chat / code, one greedy request each, thinking off, up to 512 new tokens, the MTP layer with the lookup in one tree cut by StairCut (QWEN38_FN_LOOKUP=1, as the profiles serve it). One run a cell; caches, the conductor and parallel slots off.

components.label: Conductor
components.what: Gives each request the right instructions and helper packages, and watches long sessions so they do not get stuck.
components.note: Off, clients talk to the raw engine and the small models below have nothing to do.

components.label: Narrator
components.what: A small model that writes short status lines while the big model thinks, so you can see what it is doing.
components.note: Qwen3.5-2B, 3.60 GiB in the live memory split. When memory runs short it goes after the shadow reader and loads again later.

components.label: Laya decision models
components.what: Three tiny classifiers that answer the conductor's quick questions, like what kind of request this is, in milliseconds.
components.note: Without them the big model answers those questions itself, which costs a turn each time.

components.label: Shadow reader
components.what: A small model that reads along with each session when the box is idle, so later questions about it are answered fast.
components.note: Qwen3.5-0.8B (1.52 GiB in the live memory split) and up to 4 GiB of session states (QWEN38_SHADOW_GB). The first to unload when memory runs short.

components.label: Vision
components.what: Lets the model read images you send with a message.
components.note: The tower ships inside the pack, quantised like the model (0.29 GB in 3.05; the load stage took 0.27 GiB allocated and 0.26 to 0.31 GiB of MemAvailable, VIS-97, 2026-10-12). The extra 0.5 GiB is the cache of encoded images (--image-cache-mb 512). The other packs' towers are 4 bits (2.05) or 6 (4.05 to 6.05), about 0.24 and 0.36 GB; 4.05 keeps its tower in vision_k6.safetensors beside the shards.

components.label: Conversation cache
components.what: Keeps the conversation the model is in, so the next turn starts where the last one ended instead of reading everything again.
components.note: The resident prefix with its anchors every 4,096 tokens (Flash-Next's prefill chunk), the end anchor, the pin and the park; an anchor is 110.3 MiB.

components.label: State store
components.what: Saves the model's state after short chats, so the same start a second time costs nothing.

components.label: Response cache
components.what: Answers an identical greedy request again from memory, without running the model.
components.note: Off on the reference box. Useful for scripts that send the same request many times; never for a benchmark.

components.label: Disk cache
components.what: Keeps the start of long prompts on the SSD, so a long agent session or a returning chat starts in seconds.
components.note: A folder of its own per profile (the profile file names it); a file of another fingerprint is swept.

components.label: Session spill
components.what: Moves a paused conversation to the SSD instead of dropping it, and brings it back on its next turn.
components.note: Compressed, up to SESSION_SPILL_GB (64 GB), inside the disk cache's folder.

components.label: Other backends
components.what: Lets the dashboard send some model names to other servers or cloud APIs, beside this engine.
components.note: You add the backends later, on the Backends screen.

methods.label: Thinking effort
methods.what: How long the model may think before it answers, when a client does not say.

methods.label: Default answer length
methods.what: The longest answer, in tokens, when a client does not set max_tokens.

methods.label: Request time limit
methods.what: Seconds one request may run before the engine stops it.

methods.label: Queue length
methods.what: How many requests may wait for a free slot before new ones are turned away.

methods.label: Queue wait
methods.what: Seconds a request may wait in the queue before it gets an error.

advanced.label: Port
advanced.what: The port the API and the dashboard answer on.

advanced.label: Listen on
advanced.what: The whole network, or only this machine.

advanced.label: Raw engine name
advanced.what: The model name of the raw engine. With the conductor on, clients see TandemLLM and this name is a hidden alias.

advanced.label: Dashboard login
advanced.what: With an admin password set, on makes the dashboard ask for it too.

advanced.label: Admin password
advanced.what: Without one, anyone who reaches the port can change the setup. Generate writes a random one into secrets.env on the box; read it there with cat.
